hints: Focus on what hot, concentrated, acidified manganate(VII) does to alkenes, it completely cleaves each C=C bond.
Count the C=C bonds in the termite molecule and label what is attached to each C, two alkyl groups, one H, or two H atoms.
Link each bond type to its cleavage products and check whether any fragment can give ethanoic acid.
walkthrough:
**Draw out the carbon skeleton**

Look carefully at the structure. It is a triene with three separate C=C bonds.

Left to right it is essentially $(CH_3)_2C=CH-CH_2-CH_2-C(=CH_2)-CH=CH_2$

**Recall the hot concentrated oxidation rules**

Hot, concentrated $MnO_4^- / H^+$ cleaves $C=C$ and oxidises each end fully.

$$R_2C=CR_2 \rightarrow 2 \text{ ketones}$$
$$R_2C=CHR \rightarrow \text{ ketone } + RCO_2H$$
$$R_2C=CH_2 \rightarrow \text{ ketone } + CO_2$$
$$RCH=CH_2 \rightarrow RCO_2H + CO_2$$

**Cleave the left-hand $(CH_3)_2C=CH-$ bond**

The left carbon has two $CH_3$ groups, the right carbon has one H and one alkyl chain.

$$(CH_3)_2C= \rightarrow CH_3COCH_3$$
This gives propanone, so compound 2 is formed.

**Cleave the two terminal $=CH_2$ bonds**

The middle $C(=CH_2)$ is of type $R_2C=CH_2$ and the right end $-CH=CH_2$ is of type $RCH=CH_2$.

$$=CH_2 \rightarrow CO_2$$
Both terminal methylene groups are fully oxidised to carbon dioxide, so compound 1 is formed. No $CH_3-CH=$ fragment exists to give $CH_3CO_2H$, so compound 3 is not formed.

**Conclude the product list**

Only $CO_2$ and $CH_3COCH_3$ plus larger keto-acid fragments are produced.

That is 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This claims 1, 2 and 3 are all formed. While $CO_2$ and $CH_3COCH_3$ are correct, there is no $CH_3CH=$ or $CH_3C=$ fragment that would cleave to $CH_3CO_2H$. Students choose this if they assume any substituted alkene gives ethanoic acid.
options.B: Correct. The $(CH_3)_2C=$ end gives $CH_3COCH_3$ and the two $=CH_2$ groups give $CO_2$ on vigorous oxidation. No fragment gives $CH_3CO_2H$, so only 1 and 2 are produced.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes $CH_3CO_2H$. Ethanoic acid would require a $CH_3CH=$ unit. The left end is $(CH_3)_2C=$ which gives a ketone, not an acid, and the other ends are $=CH_2$ which give $CO_2$.
options.D: Incorrect. This omits one of the true products. The trisubstituted left-hand double bond clearly gives propanone on cleavage, and the terminal alkenes clearly give $CO_2$, so both 1 and 2 must be included.
